recommendation.bottom_line: Use the free transfer to upgrade Semenyo to Gakpo for attacking upside; hold Martinez who is Chelsea's No.1 facing Hull at home in GW4; captain De Cuyper in a favourable away trip to Coventry.

transfer.rationale: Martinez has moved to Chelsea and is their starting GK (rated 8.8/10 in GW2) facing promoted Hull City at home in GW4 — a prime clean-sheet opportunity. Selling him for Tzolakis is counterproductive: Tzolakis goes AWAY to Chelsea in GW4, his hardest possible fixture, negating the 4.17 projected gain entirely for this week. Instead, use the free transfer on Semenyo → Gakpo: Liverpool's attacking output gives Gakpo multiple routes to points (goals, assists, clean sheet bonus) and net gain of 1.83 with £3.1m in bank preserved for future flexibility. No hit taken.

chip.rationale: No chip clears the threshold across any profile this week. The 139-point deficit to the rival is a season-long chase — deploying chips in GW4 with no double gameweek or exceptional fixture cluster would be premature and wasteful.

captain.rationale: Highest projected EV (1.14) among options. In GW1 he scored and forced an own goal away to Aston Villa, recording four shots and three chances created in a 4-0 win. In GW4 Brighton travel to newly promoted Coventry — a soft fixture. He is deployed out-of-position as a left winger (defender FPL price), giving clean-sheet points plus massive attacking upside. Joao Pedro (1.09 EV) is a credible alternative — Chelsea host Hull at home — but De Cuyper's price-to-EV ratio and confirmed advanced role make him the pick.

watch_outs: De Cuyper rotation risk: Brighton signed left-back Hadjam and have Conference League fixtures creating Thursday-Sunday sequences; if Kadioglu returns fit, De Cuyper could drop back to LB with reduced attacking output or be rested entirely.
Martinez (Chelsea) finger injury carried from Europa League final — no surgery required and 20-day recovery timeline noted, but monitor pre-GW4 team news for any late fitness concerns.
João Pedro minutes risk: Welbeck signed by Chelsea adds squad depth competition, though Pedro remains clear No.1 striker under Xabi Alonso.

Hull City (Tzolakis) face Chelsea away in GW4 — worst possible fixture for a newly promoted goalkeeper; any consideration of the Martinez → Tzolakis move should be deferred until GW5+ when Hull's schedule eases.

recommendation._raw_text:
I now have sufficient information to make a decisive recommendation. Key findings:

- 
Emi Martinez completed a permanent move to Chelsea from Aston Villa
, so the "Martinez" in the squad is now a Chelsea goalkeeper (confirmed by 
his Chelsea debut with four saves, and he appears set to operate as Chelsea's No. 1
).
- 
Martinez scored 8.8/10 in Chelsea's GW2 4-3 win over Brighton
, showing strong early form.
- 
Chelsea face Hull City at home on Saturday 12 September (GW4)
 — an excellent clean sheet opportunity.
- 
Tzolakis is a Hull City goalkeeper priced at £4.6m with 26 points this season
. 
He kept a clean sheet against Man Utd and Hull beat Manchester United 2-0
. His GW4 fixture is away at Chelsea — a very tough assignment.
- 
De Cuyper delivered big in GW1 — deployed out-of-position on the left wing, he forced an own goal and scored, recording four shots and three chances created
.
- 
Brighton face Coventry away in GW4
 — a very winnable fixture for De Cuyper.
- 
De Cuyper's upside has strengthened at exactly the same time his rotation risk has increased
 due to Brighton's Conference League commitments and new signing Hadjam.
- 
João Pedro was expected to be Free Hitted away in GW3 against Arsenal before staying in the GW4 squad against Hull at home
 — Chelsea host Hull in GW4, meaning João Pedro faces Hull at Stamford Bridge, a great fixture.
- 
João Pedro finished last season with 15 goals and 4 assists
.
- The Martinez → Tzolakis transfer has the highest projected net gain (4.17) across all profiles, but Tzolakis in GW4 goes AWAY to Chelsea — his toughest possible fixture. That dramatically undermines the transfer's GW4 value specifically.
- The right call is to keep Martinez (Chelsea's starting GK, home to Hull in GW4) and instead look at the Semenyo → Gakpo swap for the free transfer, given Gakpo's Liverpool attacking threat. But wait — let me check if Gakpo/Joao Pedro fixture context makes more sense for captain too.

Given Joao Pedro has the second-highest projected EV (1.09) and Chelsea host Hull at home in GW4, while De Cuyper (highest EV at 1.14) faces Coventry away — De Cuyper is the captain pick. The transfer should be Martinez → Tzolakis only if Tzolakis had a good GW4 fixture, but he faces Chelsea AWAY. Hold Martinez (Chelsea No.1, home to Hull) and use the free transfer on Semenyo → Gakpo for attacking upside.
